articles.title: Java4Shell: RCE in OpenJDK when processing Base64
articles.raw_description: A memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. Discovered and reported by Calif. After we disclosed PHP2Shell , we realized many people didn't know what PHP was. So we decided to go after something a little more familiar: Java. Today, we are disclosing Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder. OpenJDK is the most popular Java runtime. Under CVSS 4.0, this vulnerability scores 9.2 out of 10 (CRITICAL). While PHP is a high-level web technology, Java sits much deeper. Java is the world's third most popular programming language , powering 90% of Fortune 500 companies . It is the beating heart of the modern economy. Banking, aviation, telecommunications, nearly every critical sector runs on Java, including national security systems. Base64 is a very common way of representing binary data as text. It is used in authentication protocols, to encode file uploads, and to deliver network messages. To decode Base64 faster, OpenJDK uses specialized x86-64 CPU instructions to process many bytes at once. We discovered a bug in that optimized machine-level code that lets malformed input overwrite neighboring memory. With careful exploitation, the corruption can reveal sensitive memory, as Heartbleed did, or lead to remote code execution. Quad9's withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine
articles.raw_description: Quad9's forced withdrawal from France highlights the dangers of mandating DNS-level blocking. Last month, the Swiss non-profit foundation Quad9 announced Â that it will withdraw its free public DNS resolver from France. This difficult decision followed months of litigation and a French court ruling that imposed daily financial penalties on Quad9 for failing to block domains associated with alleged copyright infringement. Quad9âs departure from France is both disheartening and understandable. The courtâs ruling put the organization in the impossible bind of having to choose between crippling litigation and penalties, or fundamentally altering its service in a way that would undermine the privacy and security of its users. Left with no good option, Quad9 is choosing the exit door instead. The withdrawal of a basic infrastructure service from France fundamentally harms the free and open Internet, and it should serve as a warning of the damage that will result if rightsholders and policymakers continue demanding maximal blocking across every layer of the Internet. It not only deprives French Internet users of a trustworthy and important tool; it creates a real risk of disruption to their daily lives. ID.me terms required for IRS sign-in
articles.raw_description: IRS sign-in through ID.me: its terms require arbitration absent a 30-day opt-out; government verification data is excluded from Shop marketing, with exceptions. From Consumer Rights Wiki Taxpayers who sign in to Internal Revenue Service (IRS) online services with ID.me , a private-sector sign-in provider, [ 1 ] [ 2 ] use it under ID.me's own Terms of Service, which send disputes outside small claims court to a neutral arbitrator instead of a judge or jury unless the user opts out within 30 days of accepting them. [ 3 ] ID.me's Privacy Policy says it "may use information for marketing purposes" & may transfer information in a sale, merger or other corporate transaction, [ 4 ] though it says information from state or federal government identity verification is not used for marketing for ID.me Shop, its shopping-discount site, unless the user consents or meets another listed exception. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] Login.gov , which the U.S. government maintains, also works for IRS sign-in, [ 2 ] & the IRS's Direct Pay service takes bank-account tax payments with "No sign-in required". articles.title: Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%
articles.raw_description: Google's AI answers are taking clicks from websites in the search results. In a randomized experiment, researchers hid AI Overviews from some US desktop users. Comparing them with users who still saw Overviews shows that an Overview cuts clicks to outside websites by about 40%. Those Overviews now appear on more than half the US keywords DataForSEO tracks, up from 6% two years ago. The industry's answer, GEO (generative engine optimization), has yet to show a way to compensate for the loss. While AI citations correlate with the same kind of link profile that goes with higher Google rankings, in March AI assistants sent websites just 0.3% of their traffic.
